To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) exchange rates should not be targeted, 2) central banks should have a clear mandate for price stability, 3) monetary aggregates should not be targeted and 4) central banks should be accountable for their actions.
1) the best monetary policy regime depends on a country's institutions, and 2) the most successful monetary policies have been those that are transparent and accountable.

1) inflation targeting has worked better than the other regimes; 2) inflation targeting has not worked in every case; 3) inflation targets should be set at a low and stable rate; 4) inflation targets should not be set at zero; 5) monetary targeting has been a failure; 6) exchange rate targeting has worked in only a few cases; 7) monetary targeting is the worst of the four regimes; 8) the implicit nominal anchor has been a failure
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and under what circumstances a country can benefit from having a nominal anchor for its monetary policy.
the question of how monetary authorities in different countries have achieved the goals of price and financial stability in the context of different monetary regimes.
the question, what are the best practices for monetary policy in a particular country?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is not a unique best monetary policy regime, but that each country should find the regime that best fits its own circumstances.

the best monetary policy regime is the one that best fits the country in question.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the monetary policy regime that is best for a country is the one that it can live with.

monetary policy regimes that work best are those that have a clear and credible commitment to a nominal anchor and a clear and credible mechanism for holding policymakers accountable for achieving that anchor.
the best monetary policy is one that has a clear nominal anchor, is transparent about its goals, and is held accountable for achieving those goals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best strategy is one that is tailored to a country’s particular circumstances.
the choice of monetary policy strategy is less important for success than the institutional framework within which the strategy is implemented.
monetary policy regimes are not a one-size-fits-all proposition.
